title: Association between screen exposure and language, communication and interaction problems in early childhood
summary: To what extent are currently increasingly observable language development delays with accompanying symptoms such as restricted interaction and play behavior related to increased screen exposure during language acquisition-relevant early childhood? Is this combination of developmental delay and symptoms a newly occurring phenomenon, in the sense that one can speak of only rudimentary first language acquisition that is insufficient for further communication and written language acquisition, as has previously only been described in the literature as individual case studies in connection with massive neglect and deprivation?
conditions: Language Development Disorder, Attention Deficit Disorder, Behavioral Disorder

interventions.name: Following a clinical retrospective and explorative design, data are extracted from patient files (medical reports written by physicians and psychologists, examinations, internal documentation etc.) of children who consulted the Social Pediatric Center Schwabing of the kbo Kinderzentrum in Munich, Ge

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Children that consulted the Social Pediatric Center Schwabing with and/or due to language developmental problems.
Exclusion criteria:
Syndromes, severe diseases, intellectual disablilities, Autism Spectrum Disorder
